answer: Newcomers settle on a knoll, a registry slot whose rent is set by a shale ledger: each layer records a past deposit, and slots tied to the same payer stack new shale layers, so rent for the k-th sibling is k times the base. A gale, a surprise burst of live tasks, then hits every slot of one payer at the same instant and each must answer separately within seconds, so n fakes cost about n^2 rent plus n real concurrent compute, while an honest agent pays base rent once.
